The learning-rate multiplier at step: linear warmup, then cosine.

Written closed-form rather than as a chain of schedulers so that the whole curve is one readable expression and warmup == 0 provably reproduces the CosineAnnealingLR it replaces -- 0.5 (1 + cos(pi step / T_max)) is that scheduler's own closed form.
Every number this project has measured was trained on that curve, so a run without --warmup-frac must still be on it.

Warmup is what RSNA23 1st runs and what T011 diagnosed ConvNeXt as missing: a fresh attention pool and head at full LR in the first steps push large gradients through a pretrained encoder before anything downstream is worth listening to.
AdamW, optionally with layer-wise learning-rate decay over the encoder.
Layer-wise decay gives early backbone blocks a smaller LR than late ones, on the argument that ImageNet edge filters need less moving than the semantic layers.
It is the other half of T011's diagnosis: ConvNeXt was handed B2's recipe and came back at solo rho 0.2627 against 0.5713, and "AdamW, warmup, lower LR, layer-wise decay" is what that Result names.

Layer assignment comes from timm's own param_groups_layer_decay, which reads each architecture's group_matcher -- the point of the lane is to stop imposing one family's recipe on another, so guessing at block boundaries here would repeat the mistake in a new place.
If that helper is not importable the run stops rather than quietly training a different recipe than the one it was launched for;
a silently different recipe is exactly what T009 lost five kernels to.
The pooling, the layout embeddings and the head are not part of the pretrained stack and are trained from scratch, so they stay at full LR.

Every non-mirror view is side-neutral -- it moves no medial pixel towards lateral on any plane -- so it needs no relabeling and is valid for every study.
Only the mirror can be undefined for a study, and then that study keeps the views that are defined for it.

Test-time augmentation: what each view may do, and what it must not.
Three properties carry the weight here.

A view must be a presentation the training augmentation could have drawn, or it averages in a guess -- so every constant is checked against the sampling range of the flag it claims, and a view no checkpoint was trained through is refused before a kernel spends a minute.

The mirror is a relabeling, not a flip -- it is the one view that moves labels, and the bag-level version must reproduce the loader's version exactly, including reversing slice order on sagittal rather than flipping columns (the P0 error, which would swap anterior for posterior and take Baker's, our best label at 0.984, down with it).
The blend must divide by the weight that actually landed, because a view can be undefined for a study and for a label at once.

An absent flag must read as off;
reading it as "unspecified, allow" is how a model gets fed a presentation it has never seen and the average gets worse for free.
And the refusal is acted on, not merely computed.
The policy lives in tta.check_views rather than inside a kernel's main() for exactly this reason: a rule that only exists in a script is a rule nothing exercises.

Stated from the anatomy: on sagittal, medial-lateral is the slice index (ROADMAP, "medial-lateral lives on a different axis per plane").

--- every constant sits inside the range its flag samples -------------- Stated literally from _augment and --rotate, not read back out of the code under test: a check that asks the implementation what to expect agrees with it by construction, including when it is wrong (T015 found two of those in its own tests).

Mirror a collated bag the way the loader would have, per series.
Two things make this the same operation as the training-time mirror rather than a lookalike:
Per series, on its own geometric axis. Sagittal reverses slice order, coronal and axial flip columns (src/mirror.py).
The axis comes from the meta column emit_axis writes, never from the series CSV's plane label.
Real slices only, on the slice axis. Reversing a padded chunk would move the padding to the front while the mask still described the back.
Training mirrors before padding;
this mirrors inside the padding.
The meta is deliberately not touched.

Training assigns each slot's position after the mirror, so a mirrored sample's positions still ascend 0..1 across its real slices -- which is exactly what reversing the pixels and leaving g alone produces here.

Everything added after T009 draws here instead, so a run with none of the new flags set is bit-identical to the code that scored 0.915 -- this stream is never touched, and the old one never shifts position.

It is keyed on the epoch as well, because a mirror drawn once per study is not an augmentation: it would present half the corpus in a permanently mirrored frame rather than doubling the population, which is the entire mechanism claimed for it (T012 §4.6b).
Read every plane before flipping any of them.

Which flip a series needs depends on which knee this is, and that is a study-level fact: one series carrying the Laterality tag settles all three, so a plane whose own header lost the tag is not left un-flipped beside them.
Laterality is still voted once per study, across every series read: all of them image the same knee, so one tag settles the whole bag.
Since T013 the vote falls back to the patient-frame x-coordinate when no series carries a tag or a side word, which is what takes coverage from 57.3% of studies to 100%.
The mirror is decided once for the whole study, and the draw happens whether or not it can be used, so a study's position in its own random stream does not depend on what its headers say.
Two conditions gate it, and both are about the mirrored sample being defined.
The side must be resolved, or the study was never put in the left-knee frame and mirroring it would relabel it at random.
And every plane actually read must have a known geometric axis, because a knee cannot be mirrored on the coronal and not the sagittal: a bag half-mirrored is a bag of two different knees.
Canonicalize after the resize, not before: post-resize the tensor is size x size where the source can be 960^2, so this is a ~9x smaller copy for identical semantics.

Before the crop and while the stack still holds exactly the real slices: on sagittal this reverses slice order, and reversing a padded stack would put the padding at the front of the bag with the mask still describing the back.
Same reason as in _canonicalize: reversing slice order swaps "the slice before" for "the slice after".

Per-label loss weights travel with the target, always, rather than only when something is masked: a tensor whose width varies by sample does not collate, and a fifth element that appears only sometimes is a shape bug waiting for the first mirrored batch.
1.0 in the mask means "the report was silent here", so the weight becomes 0 and that cell stops supervising the image.
Order matters and is not interchangeable.
The at-BASE status belongs to a finding, so it has to follow that finding through the medial<->lateral swap -- permute it exactly as the target is permuted.
Only then apply MIRROR_MASK, which drops MCL because its reflection (the LCL) is not one of the 12.

mirror_weights replaces the weights it is handed rather than combining with them, so the two must be multiplied here or the at-BASE mask would be silently discarded on exactly the samples the mirror touches.
(S,H,W) -> (S,size,size), or packed (S,3,H,W) -> (S,3,size,size).
Resizing is spatial only, so the packed case folds the channel axis into the batch and unfolds it again rather than being a second code path.

The ranks are therefore taken within a fold block, and that is a confound this function cannot remove. At submission time there are no blocks -- all ten members score every test study, so ranking happens once over the whole test set.
Out of fold, each study is seen by only the one fold that held it out, so ranking within a block also silently normalizes away differences in calibration between folds.
A gain measured this way is therefore an upper bound on what rank-averaging would buy on the leaderboard: part of it is cross-fold calibration that does not exist there.

Measured thermal profile of one fold (2026-08-26, --bs 2 --grad-checkpoint): the card climbs to 80–87 °C and holds 79 W at 2190 MHz against a 3105 MHz max — i.e. it is power-capped, not thermally throttled (clocks_event_reasons.active = 0x4 SW power cap;
both sw_thermal_slowdown and hw_thermal_slowdown read Not Active even at 87 °C).
It falls to ~44 °C within 6 minutes of going idle and to ~40 °C by 15.
The hotter part of the machine is the CPU at Tctl ≈ 93 °C, which is normal for AMD.
So the constraint is about wear and noise, not about the card being in danger, and a 20-minute cooldown is comfortably enough to return it to idle temps.

Running mean of the tail epochs' weights, updated in place.
Run 2's last five epochs scored 0.8727 / 0.8662 / 0.8740 / 0.8711 / 0.8674 -- a spread of 0.0078 against a +/-0.036 noise band on 58 studies.
They are statistically indistinguishable, so "save the argmax" is selecting on noise with the same 58 studies that are our only measuring instrument.
Averaging the tail is the standard answer precisely when the tail is equivalent, which we have now measured it to be.
Integer buffers (num_batches_tracked) take the latest value rather than a mean: they are counters, and a fractional counter is not a thing.
Note what this does not do: BatchNorm running statistics are averaged along with the weights rather than recomputed over the data.

They are already running means over the same distribution and the tail epochs sit close together, so this is the cheap approximation of update_bn -- which would cost another pass over the loader, and the loader is the bottleneck.
If the averaged checkpoint ever scores worse than the argmax one by more than noise, that approximation is the first thing to suspect.

The Grad-CAM instrument's invariants (scripts/gradcam.py).
Named test_gradcam_ distinctly, per the collision note on test_t004_per_label_attention above.
These lock the properties the instrument's numbers depend on.
All of them were verified once by ad-hoc comparison while the script was written;
that evidence lived in a shell and is gone, which is exactly the gap this file exists to close.
-- norm_entropy: 0 is a point mass, 1 is uniform, and the input need not already be a distribution. cam_entropy/attn_entropy are read off this.
Reachable: norm_entropy(aw[valid]) on a study with one usable slice. log(1) is 0, so an unguarded version divides by zero here.
-- short(): every UID in this corpus shares the prefix 1.2.826.0.1.3680043.8.498., so naming files by a head-slice collided all 4,407 studies onto one filename.
The tail is where the entropy is.
-- normalize_per_slice: an all-zero map is what a padded slot becomes once the mask is applied, and it must not divide by zero.
-- the hooked layer is observed, not hard-coded, so it must resolve on a backbone that is not an efficientnet.
-- the CAM itself, end to end on a padded bag.
Padding is masked by the caller;
what must hold here is that the masked result normalizes cleanly, since padded slots are ranked and drawn from it.
-- gradient checkpointing must not disturb the hook.
A hook placed INSIDE a checkpointed segment fires again during the recomputed backward and captures the wrong tensor.

Both backbones are checked because they put the hooked layer on opposite sides of the checkpointed region: timm checkpoints an efficientnet's blocks (leaving bn2 outside) but a resnet's layer4 (which is where pick_layer lands).
-- load_model rebuilds from the checkpoint's OWN args.
A --per-label-attn checkpoint rebuilt with shared pooling localizes the wrong thing.
-- rank_slices: the full ordering, sliced separately by each consumer.
order = rank[:--topk] draws;
rank[:5] is the recorded top5_mass.
They came off one truncated array, so --topk 3 wrote the top-3 mass into a column named top5_mass and the sheet rendered it as "top-5 attention mass".

The BatchNorm double-update caution is answered. --grad-checkpoint was measured to update num_batches_tracked twice per step, and the registered question was whether that reaches the eval-time buffers.
It produced a model that is better than the reference, so whatever it moved, it did not break anything.
That caution can stop being carried as a live risk.
bs=2 removed about 93% of the discrepancy and flipped its sign. Local fold 0 now scores corpus rho 0.6451 against the archived Kaggle fold 0's 0.6336.

The correlation between the two models' behaviour rose from 0.3876 to 0.8308 — they now largely agree about which studies are positive, which is what the BatchNorm mechanism predicted would happen once the batch stopped being one study.

Zero GPU hours were spent making this. The ten checkpoints are T018's, the argmax TTA dumps are T003's, and the only new computation was 27 minutes of local inference to produce the five fold?.swa.tta.oof.csv files.
Nothing was retrained.
The gain came from noticing that two measured levers had been filed as alternatives on the strength of a budget that cites itself.
Rule-labeler tuning. Settled: no constant in it is falsifiable at n=58.
Rule going forward: ship changes justified by a mechanism and measurable at corpus level;
treat any gold-AUC movement under 0.036 as a hint, never as a result.

Everything in this file that reasons about cost is priced in Kaggle GPU-hours against a 30 h/week allowance. T022 measured local training at ~1.75 h/fold on the RTX 4070 — faster than the T4's ~2.7 h/fold, once the memory problem is handled with --bs 1 --accum 2 (activation memory scales with images through the encoder, and bs is the only knob that shrinks it without changing what the model sees).
Quota is no longer the binding constraint on training.
Sequencing the two folds instead of co-launching them saved a fold. 9 h − 4.9 h leaves ~4.1 h;
a second concurrent kernel would have hit exhaustion mid-run, and Kaggle discards the output of a kernel killed at quota exhaustion.
The estimate being 22% low is exactly the case the ordering was chosen to survive.
